## What remains uncovered, and why

**0 PARAMS rows** are never moved by any fixture.

### Not renderable offline / not audio

| area | reason and where it is tested instead |
|---|---|
| audio sleep / wake (sleep(), wake(), queued notes during sleep) | AudioEngine.sleep() returns false for an OfflineAudioContext (audio.js:1510): there is nothing to render. Behaviour is specified by contract quirks; test in T08 conformance (core state machine, silence while asleep, queued calls replayed on wake, ramp lengths 0.15 / 0.06 / 0.005 s). |
| setLowResource, drone freeze / thaw swap | the frozen loop is realtime only (drone.js:646 `!this.offline`): an offline engine plays the live drone, so a fixture could not show the swap. The loop itself (renderDroneLoop) is rendered by drone-freeze-*; the swap crossfade, cache trim and pin changes belong to T16 / T08 tests. |
| drone files mode, chordFollow | HTMLMediaElement playback is unavailable offline (drone.js:978); chordFollow needs the files mode. |
| click aux outputs 3-4, click record, MIDI clock out, MIDI direct route, recorder tap | not on the main output; conformance tests from engine-api.json (T07 / T08 / T13). |
| meters, RTA, slotLevel, analysers | not audio: tick payloads, tested against the contract schema. |
| cache / preload / estimate / pins / eviction | memory behaviour, not audio. |
| audio restart, sink change, device rate change (48 kHz) | the oracle renders 44.1 kHz offline only; T08 rate-change test (finding 16). |
| reverb build deferral (reverb.stage defer while playing), idle slot polling | realtime scheduling (audio.js:605, 790). |
| instrument params (`slots.<i>.params.*`, dynamic rows) | only cutoff / resonance (auto-filter-cutoff) are driven; the per-instrument param tables belong to the instrument tasks (T11, T12) with fixtures of their own. |

### Open points in the oracle itself

- Fixtures with `setup.live` call those event types at their time through the engine timer (first 128-frame boundary >= t); everything else is issued up front. See README, "Order of operations".
- Chromium sums node inputs in hash-set order; fixtures that run audio-rate FM are statistical for that reason alone.
